title: Three Years of Silence  (Tres años de silencio)

segments.t: Dentro, en la recepción, Graham saca del armario la maleta azul oscuro para Caleb y Hannah. Ya es viernes por la mañana, tres horas antes del mediodía. Escuchemos primero.
So our mystery Friday caller was sleeping upstairs under my attic roof all along.
Sorry for the trouble, Graham. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.
Why could you not simply hand Owen the wooden train at his front door?
Three years ago, after our grandfather died, Owen and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.
Family houses and old memories, those arguments cut deep.
We have not spoken since that Sunday. Last week I sent him one short postcard.
Asking him to meet you here on Friday at noon?
Actually, I only wrote: 'Something from Grandfather is waiting at the Linden Courtyard Inn Friday at noon.'
Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, stubborn big brother would stay home!
You know older brothers well, Graham.
Wait, were you planning to hand the clerk the bag and watch from across the street?!
That was my cowardly Monday plan... before I met all of you.
Repasemos cada intervención del diálogo con calma.
So our mystery Friday caller was sleeping upstairs under my attic roof all along.
'Así que nuestro misterioso interlocutor del viernes estuvo durmiendo arriba bajo el techo de mi ático todo el tiempo.' El cierre
all along
significa 'desde el primer momento, todo este tiempo'.
Sorry for the trouble, Graham. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.
'Perdón por las molestias, Graham. Gracias por custodiar esta maleta toda la semana.' Una disculpa cotidiana muy cortés es
Sorry for the trouble
perdón por las molestias.
Why could you not simply hand Owen the wooden train at his front door?
'¿Por qué no podías simplemente entregarle a Owen el tren de madera en la puerta de su casa?' Aquí
hand Owen
usa la palabra 'mano' como verbo: entregar en mano.
Three years ago, after our grandfather died, Owen and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.
'Hace tres años, después de morir nuestro abuelo, Owen y yo discutimos amargamente por vender la casa vieja.' Para indicar el tema de una discusión se usa
over selling
con '-ing' tras la preposición.
Family houses and old memories, those arguments cut deep.
'Casas familiares y viejos recuerdos: esas discusiones dejan huella honda.' La metáfora
cut deep
literalmente 'cortan profundo', describe heridas emocionales serias.
We have not spoken since that Sunday. Last week I sent him one short postcard.
'No hemos hablado desde aquel domingo. La semana pasada le envié una postal corta.' Para marcar el punto exacto donde empezó un silencio se combina presente perfecto con
since that Sunday
desde aquel domingo.
Asking him to meet you here on Friday at noon?
'Pidiéndole que se reuniera contigo aquí el viernes al mediodía?' Observa la estructura limpia
Asking him to meet you
pedirle a alguien que quede contigo.
Actually, I only wrote: 'Something from Grandfather is waiting at the Linden Courtyard Inn Friday at noon.'
'En realidad, solo escribí: Algo del abuelo te espera en la posada Linden Courtyard Inn el viernes al mediodía.' Recordemos que 'esperar a alguien' es siempre 'wait for', y aquí
is waiting at
indica dónde aguarda el objeto.
Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, stubborn big brother would stay home!
'¡Ajá! ¡Temías que, si firmabas con tu nombre, el hermano mayor cabezota se quedara en casa!' Con la palabra 'home' tras verbos de estancia o movimiento no se pone preposición:
would stay home
se quedaría en casa.
You know older brothers well, Graham.
'Conoces bien a los hermanos mayores, Graham.' El adverbio de modo va detrás del objeto en inglés:
know older brothers well
nunca entre el verbo y 'hermanos'.
Wait, were you planning to hand the clerk the bag and watch from across the street?!
'¡Espera, ¿planeabas darle la maleta al recepcionista y mirar desde el otro lado de la calle?!' La combinación espacial
from across the street
sitúa la mirada justo en la acera de enfrente.
That was my cowardly Monday plan... before I met all of you.
'Ese era mi plan cobarde del lunes... antes de conocerlos a todos ustedes.' Aunque termine en '-ly',
cowardly
es un adjetivo que significa 'cobarde'. Volvamos a escuchar toda la escena de corrido.
So our mystery Friday caller was sleeping upstairs under my attic roof all along.
Sorry for the trouble, Graham. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.
Why could you not simply hand Owen the wooden train at his front door?
Three years ago, after our grandfather died, Owen and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.
Family houses and old memories, those arguments cut deep.
We have not spoken since that Sunday. Last week I sent him one short postcard.
Asking him to meet you here on Friday at noon?
Actually, I only wrote: 'Something from Grandfather is waiting at the Linden Courtyard Inn Friday at noon.'
Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, stubborn big brother would stay home!
You know older brothers well, Graham.
Wait, were you planning to hand the clerk the bag and watch from across the street?!
That was my cowardly Monday plan... before I met all of you.
En vez de esconderse al otro lado de la calle, Caleb tiene tres horas para reunir valor y quedarse aquí mismo en el patio. Nos vemos en la siguiente escena.
See you later!
